Bitdeer Technologies.why: converts its ~3 GW powered-land portfolio into AI data-center capacity: a 16-year, ~$4.7 billion colocation lease at Tydal, Norway (121 IT MW for NVIDIA GPUs) and its own Bitdeer AI GPU cloud (NVIDIA GB300 / Vera Rubin) - its revenue grows directly with AI compute build-out
Bitdeer Technologies.evidence: Bitdeer Technologies Q2 FY2026 (08-10-2026), CSO Haris Basit: subsidiary Tydal Data Center AS executed a 16-year colocation lease and services agreement with Volta at the Tydal campus, delivering 121 IT MW configured to run NVIDIA GPUs, approximately $4.7 billion in contracted base-term revenue

players.product: AI data-center colocation (Tydal, Norway: 121 IT MW leased to Volta for NVIDIA GPUs) and Bitdeer AI GPU cloud (NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 / Vera Rubin capacity in Malaysia, Norway and the US)

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 (CFO Michael Potter): revenue approximately $228.8 million, up approximately 47% year-over-year and approximately 21% sequentially, driven primarily by self-mining hash rate expansion and higher Bitcoin production plus accelerating AI Cloud contribution - AI Cloud revenue $14 million, up approximately 284% sequentially. Gross profit -$8.5 million (gross margin approximately -3.7%), a $30.5 million sequential improvement; adjusted EBITDA approximately $31.1 million, up approximately 575% year-over-year and 116% sequentially; operating loss $101.7 million.
quarterly_data.figure: revenue ~$228.8 million (+47% Y/Y, +21% Q/Q); AI Cloud $14 million (+284% Q/Q); adjusted EBITDA ~$31.1 million

quarterly_data.signal: Tydal, Norway colocation lease (CSO Haris Basit): subsidiary Tydal Data Center AS executed a 16-year colocation lease and services agreement with Volta, delivering 121 IT MW supported by approximately 133 gross MW across four existing data halls configured to run NVIDIA GPUs; approximately $4.7 billion contracted base-term revenue over the initial 16-year term (approximately $8 billion over 24 years if the eight-year renewal is exercised; tenant termination right at the end of year 10). Modified gross lease with a 3% annual escalator and electricity fully passed through; expected average annual revenue of approximately $2.4 million per IT MW. Remaining capex approximately $500 million, to be funded with project-level financing; delivery targeted in two equal phases on December 31, 2026 and March 31, 2027; PUE approximately 1.1, 100% renewable. CFO: the site has 180 gross MW in total, of which 47 MW gross is retained for Bitdeer's own AI Cloud.
quarterly_data.figure: 121 IT MW (~133 gross MW); ~$4.7 billion over 16 years (~$8 billion over 24 years); ~$2.4 million per IT MW per year; remaining capex ~$500 million

quarterly_data.signal: AI Cloud (CFO): annual recurring revenue approximately $76 million at end of June, up approximately 77% quarter-over-quarter; utilization approximately 95% across 4,248 deployed GPUs; signed a new 10-year lease for 21.7 IT MW in Malaysia (handover expected Q1 2027) designed to support 128 NVIDIA GB300 NVL72 systems. CFO: existing GPUs in Asia are quite used up. CEO Jihan Wu: near-term GPU deployment is mostly in Malaysia, demand is very strong and usually multi-year, and the bottleneck right now is Bitdeer's own execution; Norway (a little less than 15 MW reserved for itself) follows, expected within next year, then US data centers in Tennessee and Washington. CEO: GPU contract discussions now focus on long-term contracts of five years.
quarterly_data.figure: AI Cloud ARR ~$76 million (+77% Q/Q); ~95% utilization on 4,248 GPUs; 21.7 IT MW Malaysia lease for 128 GB300 NVL72 systems

quarterly_data.signal: Power portfolio approximately 3 GW of total global electrical capacity at end of Q2, up approximately 12% year-over-year (CSO). Guidance (CFO): full-year 2026 crypto mining infrastructure capex revised to $200 million-$280 million on additional North American infrastructure opportunities; this excludes capex for SEALMINER hardware, GPUs, AI Cloud or colocation development. Massillon, Ohio has 174 MW online for mining; Fox Creek, Alberta broke ground in June - a $155 million investment including a fully permitted 101 MW on-site natural gas power plant with grid interconnection.
quarterly_data.figure: ~3 GW power portfolio (+12% Y/Y); 2026 mining infrastructure capex $200 million-$280 million

quarterly_data.signal: Bitcoin mining and SEALMINER (CFO): self-mining hash rate approximately 73 EH/s at end of Q2, up approximately 342% year-over-year, on approximately 243,000 active self-mining rigs; Q2 production approximately 2,694 Bitcoin (+377% year-over-year); co-mining hash rate grew over 260% sequentially. SEALMINER A4 Ultra Hydro operates at 9.45 J/TH at chip level; launched SEALMINER DL1 Hydro for Scrypt mining. Broke ground in July on a 187,000 sq ft SEALMINER manufacturing facility in Sparks, Nevada, expected complete by end of 2026 with capacity of 10,000 units per month. Existing wafer inventory is designated for internal use.
quarterly_data.figure: ~73 EH/s (+342% Y/Y); ~2,694 BTC in Q2; Sparks NV plant 10,000 units/month by end-2026
